about: The bench leg's baseline (tools/bench_leg.sh, #137; S3, lane gate-137, 2026-10-14). Every number is [M], read from the record named beside it. A wall more than `bar` times its baseline AND more than `floor_seconds` above it is RED. The bar, the floor and every baseline are re-cut only by a dated commit that names the records it read; the cut below is the one of 2026-10-14, read beside #117's table (docs/records/20261014-212357-speed-117-s3.md, sections 1.1, 2 and 3, on lane/speed-117 at 044243a0), which quotes the same records. The `rerun` field of a chain executable wall (lane cold-137, #137, 2026-10-15) is the command tools/chain_leg.sh runs for it, read by the cold-run rule of tools/bench_leg.sh; it moves no baseline.
floor_why: [M] the box walls of the sub-second chain executables move by more than 1.5 times between GREEN runs at nearby commits (finalitycheck 0.021991 s at docs/records/20261014-124337-make-check-box.txt:508, 0.156361 s at docs/records/20261014-200321-make-check-box.txt:509); the floor keeps that noise from turning the tripwire RED while a wall of a second or more is held to the bar

box.how: per wall, the largest of the three newest box tripwire records of 2026-10-14 (20261014-193207, 20261014-200321, 20261014-211019), the record and line named; the harness and fuzz walls from this lane's record docs/records/20261014-212637-bench-baseline-gate-137.md (the tripwire records carry each binary's in-process wall at 0.1 s resolution, e.g. docs/records/20261014-211019-make-check-box.txt:405/407/409; the harness timing lines time the whole `cargo run`, a different measure, so they are baselined from this lane's record); the in-process walls of run_diff and run_engine gosdk/tssdk, the largest of the same three records, are read from the binaries' own trailing wall (the record indents each line by two spaces, the tripwire's log does not)
